note: Every fixture is a project at some layout state. The skill must resolve the format before it writes anything, hand an old layout to stack-it:migrate rather than restructuring it, and keep generated stack content out of CLAUDE.md in every case. Fixtures for stop cases (foreign-stack-doc, format-ahead-of-plugin) hold only the files that trigger the stop, since the skill halts in Step 1 before it reads the stack.

evals.name: from-lockfile
evals.prompt: I want my project's tech stack documented so both my coding agents and new contributors know what we're using and how to run things. Put the agent-facing reference where any agent will find it, and the human-facing part in the README. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Format resolves to 2 off the lockfile's format key (no docs/stack.md yet), so migrate does not run. Documents from .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml, which validates, with versions matching it exactly. Writes the whole of docs/stack.md, first line '> Generated by stack-it document-stack, format 2. Edits are overwritten on the next run.', carrying tools with pinned versions, the real npm build/test/lint/dev commands, the Tailwind-v4-via-Vite-plugin and flat-ESLint conventions (eslint.config.js is present as evidence), and the Vite-7-needs-Node-20.19+ caveat. Creates AGENTS.md with exactly the pointer line 'Before adding a dependency or running the build, test, or lint toolchain, read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md', path NOT in backticks, no HTML markers. Creates CLAUDE.md containing the single line '@AGENTS.md' and no generated stack content. Creates the README with a Tech Stack section + Getting Started inside a <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> managed block with the 'generated/overwritten' note.

evals.name: infer-from-codebase
evals.prompt: There's no stack file for this project. Can you figure out what it's built with and document it? I want a reference my coding agents will pick up, and a tech stack + getting started in the README. If you need me to confirm what you inferred, treat this message as the confirmation and go ahead. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: No docs/stack.md, no lockfile, and no marker block in CLAUDE.md, so there is no format signal at all and nothing to migrate. The stack is inferred from the codebase (pyproject.toml + imports): Python >=3.12, FastAPI 0.115.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, uvicorn 0.34.0, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0. The package manager is a guess and must be flagged as one: the [dependency-groups] table points at uv or another PEP 735 aware manager, and there is no uv.lock to settle it, so naming uv flatly is wrong. States plainly that the stack was inferred and what it was inferred from; does NOT fabricate a stack.yaml. Writes docs/stack.md whole with the format 2 header and the real run commands (uv run pytest, ruff check, uvicorn app.main:app), creates AGENTS.md with the single pointer line, creates CLAUDE.md as the one-line '@AGENTS.md' bridge, and creates the README with its managed block.

evals.name: idempotent-refresh
evals.prompt: The stack changed. Please re-document it. The stack reference and the README section already exist; just bring them up to date. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Both signals read 2, the docs/stack.md header and the lockfile's format key, so migrate must NOT run. The content is STALE: docs/stack.md has the format 2 header but old facts (FastAPI 0.110.0, no uvicorn/Ruff), and the README's <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> block is stale too. Human-written prose lives in AGENTS.md (House rules, Deployment notes) and outside the README markers (Contributing). Re-running must (a) overwrite docs/stack.md whole to match the lockfile (FastAPI 0.115.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, uvicorn 0.34.0, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0, Python 3.14.3), keeping the format 2 header line, (b) refresh only what's between the README markers and preserve the prose outside them verbatim, with exactly one marker pair and no second block appended, (c) leave AGENTS.md untouched, since it already contains @docs/stack.md, and leave the one-line '@AGENTS.md' CLAUDE.md alone, (d) put no generated stack content into CLAUDE.md. Run it twice and the second run produces the same header line, the same tools and versions, and no accumulated or duplicated content. This is the skill's headline idempotency property.

evals.name: agents-md-has-human-rules
evals.prompt: Document this project's stack for the agents and for people, then do it again to check nothing drifts. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: AGENTS.md already holds human-written rules (function components only, co-located tests, second reviewer for src/api/, never commit .env) AND the pointer line. Across two consecutive runs: AGENTS.md ends with exactly ONE 'read the stack reference: @docs/stack.md' line and every human rule verbatim, in its original order, with the pointer still last and still unbackticked. The presence check is on '@docs/stack.md', so the skill appends nothing even though it did not write that sentence itself. docs/stack.md is overwritten both runs and shows the same header line, the same tools and versions, and no accumulated content (Vite 7.1.0, React 19.1.0, TypeScript 5.7.3, Tailwind 4.1.11, Vitest 3.2.0, ESLint 9.17.0 with flat config from eslint.config.js). The one-line '@AGENTS.md' CLAUDE.md is left alone both runs and never receives stack content. The README's managed block is created on run one and refreshed in place on run two, never duplicated.

evals.name: from-v1-layout
evals.prompt: Please re-document this project's stack. If you need my OK to add an import line to CLAUDE.md, the answer is yes. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: Both readable signals say 1: .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml has no format key, and CLAUDE.md carries the marker block. There is no docs/stack.md, so the highest signal is 1. The skill must INVOKE stack-it:migrate rather than restructuring the layout itself, then continue once migrate reports 'migrated to 2'. End state: no <!-- stack-it:stack start/end --> block anywhere in CLAUDE.md; CLAUDE.md starts with '@AGENTS.md' (the user said yes) followed by the House rules and Deployment notes prose intact; stack.yaml stamped 'format: 2' as its first key and still valid; docs/stack.md regenerated from the lockfile with the format 2 header (FastAPI 0.115.0, SQLModel 0.0.22, uvicorn 0.34.0, pytest 8.3.0, Ruff 0.8.0, Python 3.14.3), NOT the stale 0.110.0 text that was in the old block; AGENTS.md carrying the pointer line; the README block refreshed to the uv commands. Exactly one layout at the end, never both. The report says migrate ran and what it moved.

evals.name: foreign-stack-doc
evals.prompt: Document this project's stack. The project is at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: docs/stack.md exists but was written by hand: its first line is '# Our stack, and why', not the generated header. The ownership rule must STOP the run there and ask the user before touching the file, showing what's in it. It must NOT go on to use the other signals, which both read 1 (the lockfile has no format key, CLAUDE.md carries a marker block) and would start a migration. Nothing is written: docs/stack.md is not overwritten, the CLAUDE.md block is still there with the House rules and Deployment notes around it, no AGENTS.md is created, no README is created. A cut CLAUDE.md block is the visible sign of the failure this pins, which is clobbering a human's hand-maintained stack document.

evals.name: format-ahead-of-plugin
evals.prompt: Bring the stack docs up to date for the project at PROJECT_DIR.
evals.expected_output: docs/stack.md carries a valid generated header reading 'format 3' while .claude/stack-it/stack.yaml says 'format: 2'. Reading every signal and taking the highest gives 3, which is ahead of the current format 2, so the skill stops and writes nothing and tells the user a newer stack-it wrote this project and the plugin should be upgraded. It must not downgrade the file, not overwrite docs/stack.md, and not settle on the lockfile's 2 because it looks current. migrate is not invoked. The mirror case matters just as much: a lockfile stamped 3 with a docs/stack.md still reading 2 must stop for the same reason.

evals.name: recorded-decline-not-reasked
evals.prompt: Re-document the stack for the project at PROJECT_DIR, then run it once more.
evals.expected_output: CLAUDE.md holds the user's own prose plus the pointer line, the recorded fallback from a run where they declined the '@AGENTS.md' import. AGENTS.md is the pointer-only file stack-it created. Across two runs the skill must NOT ask about the import again: the 'already contains @docs/stack.md outside backticks' case matches before the ask, so CLAUDE.md is left alone both times, with no '@AGENTS.md' line added and no second pointer line appended. docs/stack.md is refreshed from the lockfile with the format 2 header, AGENTS.md is untouched, and the README block is refreshed in place.
